# Review 01

> Status: pending-dev
> Date: 2026-04-22
> Reviewer: Code Review Agent
> Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES

## Scope

Reviewed branch `feat/entire-review` against `main`. The feature introduces a new
`entire review` command that runs configured review skills inside a single
agent session, with the session/checkpoint metadata recording that a review
occurred.

- 17 commits, ~1,750 lines across 30 files (code + tests + CLAUDE.md).
- Key files: `cmd/entire/cli/review.go` (+685), `cmd/entire/cli/review_test.go`
  (+395), `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go` + test (+186), plus additions to
  `session.State`, `settings.EntireSettings.Review`, `checkpoint` types (`Kind`,
  `ReviewSkills`, `HasReview`), `trailers`, and three agent `Launcher` impls.
- `mise run test` — all packages pass.
- `mise run lint` — 0 issues.

Previous PR-level reviewer feedback (commit `47eb589` "Address PR review
feedback") has been addressed. No prior `review-NN.md` files exist in this
repo; this is the first file-based review.

## High (Must Fix)

1. **High: the unsupported-launcher fallback clears the pending marker it
   just told the user to rely on.** In
   [review.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/review.go:414),
   the cleanup `defer` is installed before the `LauncherFor` check, and the
   fallback path at
   [review.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/review.go:425)
   returns `nil`. That means configs for non-launchable agents print
   "falling back to --track-only", but the marker is removed on return, so
   the manually started review session will not be tagged or condensed as a
   review.

   Fix: either skip the defer-driven cleanup on this branch (e.g. move the
   "fallback to track-only" return *above* the defer, analogous to how the
   `trackOnly` branch at line 400-406 already does), or short-circuit the
   cleanup with a local flag (`markerHandedOff := false; defer ... if !markerHandedOff ...`).
   Add a test that registers a non-Launcher agent and asserts the marker
   survives when `LauncherFor` returns `ok=false`.

## Important (Should Fix)

2. **Medium: `entire review` never verifies that hooks are installed for
   the configured agent before launching it.** The command selects an
   agent from settings in
   [review.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/review.go:353)
   and immediately writes the marker / launches, but there is no
   `AreHooksInstalled` gate even though the feature depends on
   `UserPromptSubmit` adoption and the repo already has
   [GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_worktree1/cmd/entire/cli/config.go:85).
   A manually edited config such as `"claude-code": [...]` in a repo
   without `entire enable` will appear to run successfully, but no review
   metadata will ever be recorded because no hook fires.

   Focused tests passed: `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/... -run 'Review|AdoptPendingReviewMarker|DetectBaseBranch|DetectReviewScope'`
   and `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/... -run 'LaunchCmd|LauncherFor'`.
   Those scenarios are not currently covered by tests.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:451-468] Multi-agent review config silently
  prefers the alphabetically-first agent, with no override.**
  `selectReviewAgent` picks `sort.Strings(names)[0]`, so a user with
  `{"claude-code": [...], "codex": [...]}` configured can never reach the
  codex agent without removing `claude-code` from settings. The doc comment
  admits "v1: single agent" but there's no flag to select an agent, and the
  first-run picker happily writes multiple entries. Either (a) gate the
  picker to one agent at a time, (b) add `--agent <name>`, or (c) prompt
  the user when the map has multiple keys. Today the UX is "I configured
  codex and nothing happens," which will produce confused bug reports.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:425 → .github/hooks, etc.] Stale config can
  point to an uninstalled agent.**
  `runReviewConfigPicker` correctly gates to `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled`,
  but once saved, `runReview` reads `s.Review` directly with no re-check.
  If the user later runs `entire disable` for an agent, its entry stays in
  the settings map, `selectReviewAgent` will pick it, and the marker will be
  written for an agent whose hook will never adopt it — same silent failure
  as the Critical above. Suggest intersecting `s.Review` keys with
  `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled(ctx)` inside `runReview` and skipping/warning
  on missing entries.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:196-201] Empty-installed-agents error message
  assumes the fix is `entire enable`.**
  The error says: `"no agents installed; run 'entire enable' first"`. In
  practice a user who disabled a specific agent via `entire configure
  --remove` may already have `entire enable`d the repo — they just don't
  have hooks for any agent. Consider `"no agents with hooks installed; run
  'entire configure --agent <name>' to install hooks."`.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/committed.go:440-449] `HasReview` is not
  derived from session metadata — stale summaries can never lose it, but
  also never gain it on rewrite.**
  `writeCheckpointSummary` carries `HasReview` forward from the existing
  summary OR sets it from `opts.HasReview`. `reaggregateFromEntries`
  recomputes `CheckpointsCount`/`FilesTouched`/`TokenUsage` by reading each
  session's `CommittedMetadata` from the tree, but **does not** look at the
  per-session `Kind` field. That means:
  1. If the summary is ever rebuilt without `opts.HasReview=true` (e.g.
     someone re-runs `CondenseSession` for a non-review session after a
     review session was previously condensed), the flag *is* preserved via
     the "existing summary" read — good.
  2. But if the root `metadata.json` blob is missing or unreadable while
     the session subfolder with `Kind=agent_review` survives, `HasReview`
     silently resets to false.
  This is unlikely in practice (the summary and session are written in the
  same commit), but the truth-of-record should be the per-session
  `CommittedMetadata.Kind`. Consider making `reaggregateFromEntries`
  OR `writeCheckpointSummary` iterate the per-session metadata and
  OR-in `Kind.IsReview()` equivalent. (Since `checkpoint` can't import
  `session`, this would mean either hardcoding `"agent_review"` in the
  checkpoint package or adding a small `IsReviewKind(string) bool` helper
  exported from `session` that's safe for `checkpoint` to consume.)

- **README.md + CHANGELOG.md — feature is undocumented for end users.**
  CLAUDE.md has extensive documentation, but `README.md` lists every other
  `entire` command in the Commands Reference table and doesn't mention
  `entire review`. `CHANGELOG.md` has no entry for this feature. If the
  command is intentionally preview/hidden, mark the cobra command
  `Hidden: true` and add a changelog "preview" note. Otherwise, add a
  README section and a CHANGELOG entry before release.

## Suggestions (Consider)

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:54-60] `pendingMarkerPath` discards
  `session.SessionStateDirName` collision risk.**
  The marker lives next to per-session `<session-id>.json` files under
  `.git/entire-sessions/`. The filename is a constant (`review-pending.json`)
  that could collide with a real session ID. Validation prevents
  path-traversal, but defense-in-depth: pick a reserved prefix (e.g.
  `.review-pending.json`) that session-ID validation would reject anyway.
  Very low risk — session IDs are `YYYY-MM-DD-<UUID>` — but a future refactor
  that loosens validation could expose this.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:126-139] `curatedReviewSkills` is a hardcoded
  map with no update path.**
  Only `claude-code` and `codex` have curated skills. New agents (or new
  skills for existing ones) require a code change. Consider loading from an
  embed-ed JSON or from agent-specific files so community skills can ship
  without a CLI release.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:481-491] `currentHeadSHA` duplicates git logic
  already available via `go-git`.**
  The rest of the codebase uses `git.PlainOpen(...).Head()`. Shelling out
  is not wrong here (consistency with `detectReviewScope`), but the helper
  could be a one-liner `repo.Head().Hash().String()` without spawning a
  subprocess. Minor.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:195-292] `runReviewConfigPicker` does not test
  coverage for accessible mode.**
  `NewAccessibleForm` is used, but no test exercises the `ACCESSIBLE=1`
  path, so regressions in accessible rendering would slip through. A
  lightweight test that sets `ACCESSIBLE=1` and verifies the form doesn't
  panic would be worth adding.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:271-289] Non-atomic read-modify-write on
  session state during marker adoption.**
  Load → mutate → Save with no lock around the file. If two concurrent
  `UserPromptSubmit` hooks adopt simultaneously, both could win because the
  first save is clobbered by the second. Concurrent hooks for the same
  session ID are unlikely in practice (agents serialize hooks per turn),
  but adding a quick `fcntl`-style advisory lock would be cheap insurance.
  Same shape of issue exists elsewhere in the codebase, so not a blocker.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:451-468] `selectReviewAgent` returns
  `([]string(nil), errors.New("..."))` twice with the same error text.**
  Collapse the two branches into a single "filter to valid entries, then
  sort" step to avoid the duplicated error string.

- **[cmd/entire/cli/review.go:302-318] Flag documentation drift risk.**
  The command `Long` text mentions `--edit` but not `--track-only`. Easy
  fix: mention `--track-only` in the long description, or trust the flag
  registration to speak for itself.

## Praise

- **Excellent defensive commentary throughout `review.go`.** Almost every
  non-trivial decision is justified in a comment — the worktree-scoped
  marker rationale (lines 141-147, 173-179), the settings-wipe data-loss
  guard (lines 330-341, 667-684), the defer-cleanup lifecycle (lines
  408-422). This raises the bar for future maintainers. Exactly the "teach
  via code" pattern the reviewer guide asks for.

- **Worktree-scoped marker is a real correctness win.**
  `TestAdoptPendingReviewMarker_OtherWorktreeLeavesMarker` documents a race
  that's hard to see until you hit it. The fix is minimal and the test
  pins it — textbook.

- **HasReview-via-Kind derivation.**
  `session.Kind.IsReview()` + `opts.HasReview: state.Kind.IsReview()` is
  the right seam. Pins the invariant that new review kinds won't need
  three string-literal updates across packages. `TestKindIsReview` makes
  it load-bearing.

- **Settings-malformed → surface error instead of clobbering.**
  `TestSaveReviewConfig_ReturnsErrorOnMalformedSettings` is exactly the
  regression shape you want pinned: the test asserts the file is byte-for-
  byte identical before and after a failed save. That's the difference
  between a close call and a data-loss bug.

- **`detectBaseBranch` fallback order matches its doc comment, and is
  tested.** Two regression tests
  (`TestDetectBaseBranch_UsesOriginMainWhenNoLocalMain`,
  `TestDetectBaseBranch_PrefersAllRemotesOverLocals`) pin the order so a
  future refactor can't quietly flip it. The
  `masterBaseBranch`/`defaultBaseBranch` constants are used consistently
  across `git_operations.go`, `resume.go`, `review.go`.

- **`Launcher` abstraction is cleanly scoped.** Three agent impls; a
  single-line Launcher interface; `LauncherFor` is the exact ergonomic
  helper callers need; `TestLauncher_AtLeastOneImplementor` ensures the
  build can't regress into a state where no agent can be spawned.

## Summary

The feature is well-engineered, thoroughly tested (394 lines of tests for
the review package alone, plus integration via `TestAdoptPendingReviewMarker*`
in `lifecycle_test.go`), and the design choices (pending-marker + hook
adoption, worktree scoping, HasReview umbrella flag, settings-malformed
guard) reflect careful thinking. CLAUDE.md is updated correctly; lint +
unit tests are green.

The High item — marker erasure on the `LauncherFor` `!ok` branch — is a
real bug that will silently break the fallback code path the commit
messages explicitly promise. It's a one-line fix plus a test. The Medium
item — no `AreHooksInstalled` gate — is the same silent-failure shape on
a different input path (manually edited config in a repo without
`entire enable`).

The other "Important" items are quality-of-release issues (multi-agent
selection UX, stale config, README/CHANGELOG). None block merge in the
strict sense, but the README/CHANGELOG gap will produce a version shipping
an undocumented command.

Estimated effort to address feedback: 2-3 hours (Critical fix + test + one
Important + docs).

### Previous Review Status

No prior `review-NN.md` files. Upstream PR-review feedback ("data-loss,
cleanup, context, HasReview derivation," commit `47eb589`) appears fully
addressed based on the current code and the dedicated regression tests:

- [x] Settings-load errors no longer wipe user config (tested).
- [x] Pending marker cleaned up on every spawn-path failure (via defer) —
      *except* the `LauncherFor !ok` branch. See Critical above.
- [x] `detectBaseBranch` prefers all remotes before any local (tested).
- [x] `HasReview` derived from `session.Kind.IsReview()` (tested).
- [x] Context threaded through marker I/O.
- [x] `headHasReviewCheckpoint` logs at Debug on each failure step.

I read the review against the actual code. Here's my take on which findings hold up.

## Agree — real issues

**High: marker-wipe on the `LauncherFor !ok` fallback is a real bug.** Verified at `cmd/entire/cli/review.go:414-429`:

- The `trackOnly` branch returns at line 406, *before* the cleanup defer at line 414 — safe.
- The `!ok` branch at line 425-430 returns *after* the defer is registered. The defer reads the marker, sees it exists (no hook ran), and clears it at line 419. So the user is told "falling back to --track-only, start the agent manually" but the marker the manually-started agent needs for adoption is gone.
- `copilotcli`, `cursor`, `factoryaidroid`, `opencode`, `vogon` all exist in `agent/` without `LaunchCmd`, so the path is reachable.

Fix shape is as the reviewer described — either move the `!ok` return before the defer (mirror the `trackOnly` structure), or add a `markerHandedOff` flag the defer checks.

**Medium: no `AreHooksInstalled` gate before launch.** Confirmed — `runReview` goes straight from `settings.Load` → `selectReviewAgent` → `WritePendingReviewMarker` with no intersection against `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled`. Same silent-failure class as the High (marker written, no hook ever fires to adopt it). The picker does gate, but saved config can go stale once the user runs `entire disable` for an agent.

**Multi-agent silent preference.** `selectReviewAgent` at `review.go:451-468` is `sort.Strings(names)[0]`, and `newReviewCmd` at 315-316 registers only `--edit` and `--track-only`. A user with `{"claude-code": [...], "codex": [...]}` can't reach codex without editing settings.json. Valid.

**HasReview not derived from per-session `Kind` in `reaggregateFromEntries`.** Confirmed at `checkpoint/committed.go:434-462` — aggregation doesn't read per-session `Kind`, so the flag rides on carry-forward + `opts.HasReview`. Reviewer correctly notes the practical risk is low (summary + session written same commit), but the invariant is weaker than the `Kind.IsReview()` seam suggests.

## Partial agree

**Stale config pointing at uninstalled agent.** Same root cause as the Medium above; fixing one should fix both (intersect `s.Review` keys with `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` inside `runReview`).

**README / CHANGELOG.** Worth verifying before shipping — if it's intentionally preview, `Hidden: true` on the cobra command is the cheap signal.

## Less important

The suggestions (marker filename collision, curated-skills hardcoding, `currentHeadSHA` shelling out, accessible-mode test, non-atomic state write) are all reasonable follow-ups but none are blockers.

## Priority if you act on this

1. Fix the High — one-line reorder + one test (~15 min).
2. Add `--agent` flag and gate `runReview` on `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` (addresses Medium + stale-config + multi-agent UX in one pass).
3. README/CHANGELOG or `Hidden: true`.
4. Everything else can wait.

# Simplify: Code Review and Cleanup

Review all changed files for reuse, quality, and efficiency. Fix any issues found.

## Phase 1: Identify Changes

Run `git diff` (or `git diff HEAD` if there are staged changes) to see what changed. If there are no git changes, review the most recently modified files that the user mentioned or that you edited earlier in this conversation.

## Phase 2: Launch Three Review Agents in Parallel

Use the Agent tool to launch all three agents concurrently in a single message. Pass each agent the full diff so it has the complete context.

### Agent 1: Code Reuse Review

For each change:

1. **Search for existing utilities and helpers** that could replace newly written code. Look for similar patterns elsewhere in the codebase — common locations are utility directories, shared modules, and files adjacent to the changed ones.
2. **Flag any new function that duplicates existing functionality.** Suggest the existing function to use instead.
3. **Flag any inline logic that could use an existing utility** — hand-rolled string manipulation, manual path handling, custom environment checks, ad-hoc type guards, and similar patterns are common candidates.

### Agent 2: Code Quality Review

Review the same changes for hacky patterns:

1. **Redundant state**: state that duplicates existing state, cached values that could be derived, observers/effects that could be direct calls
2. **Parameter sprawl**: adding new parameters to a function instead of generalizing or restructuring existing ones
3. **Copy-paste with slight variation**: near-duplicate code blocks that should be unified with a shared abstraction
4. **Leaky abstractions**: exposing internal details that should be encapsulated, or breaking existing abstraction boundaries
5. **Stringly-typed code**: using raw strings where constants, enums (string unions), or branded types already exist in the codebase
6. **Unnecessary JSX nesting**: wrapper Boxes/elements that add no layout value — check if inner component props (flexShrink, alignItems, etc.) already provide the needed behavior
7. **Nested conditionals**: ternary chains (`a ? x : b ? y : ...`), nested if/else, or nested switch 3+ levels deep — flatten with early returns, guard clauses, a lookup table, or an if/else-if cascade
8. **Unnecessary comments**: comments explaining WHAT the code does (well-named identifiers already do that), narrating the change, or referencing the task/caller — delete; keep only non-obvious WHY (hidden constraints, subtle invariants, workarounds)

### Agent 3: Efficiency Review

Review the same changes for efficiency:

1. **Unnecessary work**: redundant computations, repeated file reads, duplicate network/API calls, N+1 patterns
2. **Missed concurrency**: independent operations run sequentially when they could run in parallel
3. **Hot-path bloat**: new blocking work added to startup or per-request/per-render hot paths
4. **Recurring no-op updates**: state/store updates inside polling loops, intervals, or event handlers that fire unconditionally — add a change-detection guard so downstream consumers aren't notified when nothing changed. Also: if a wrapper function takes an updater/reducer callback, verify it honors same-reference returns (or whatever the "no change" signal is) — otherwise callers' early-return no-ops are silently defeated
5. **Unnecessary existence checks**: pre-checking file/resource existence before operating (TOCTOU anti-pattern) — operate directly and handle the error
6. **Memory**: unbounded data structures, missing cleanup, event listener leaks
7. **Overly broad operations**: reading entire files when only a portion is needed, loading all items when filtering for one

## Phase 3: Fix Issues

Wait for all three agents to complete. Aggregate their findings and fix each issue directly. If a finding is a false positive or not worth addressing, note it and move on — do not argue with the finding, just skip it.

content.text:
## What `entire review` does

It runs a set of configured review skills inside a single agent session, and records — permanently, on the next `git commit` — that the code was reviewed and which skills were run. The review metadata rides along in the checkpoint alongside normal session metadata.

It does **not** track verdicts, status, or create empty commits. The session is just a fact, attached to whatever commit you make next.

## The core idea: pending-marker + hook adoption

The command doesn't launch the agent and inject a special mode. Instead:

1. `entire review` writes a small "pending review" marker file to `.git/entire-sessions/review-pending.json` — just the agent name, selected skills, starting SHA, worktree path, and a timestamp.
2. It spawns (or tells you to manually start) the agent.
3. When the agent fires its first `UserPromptSubmit` lifecycle hook, the hook handler calls `adoptPendingReviewMarkerInto`, which:
   - Reads the marker.
   - Checks the marker's `WorktreePath` matches the session's — so a marker written in worktree A isn't claimed by a session in worktree B (both share `.git/entire-sessions/`).
   - Tags the session with `Kind = session.KindAgentReview` and stores the skills in `state.ReviewSkills`.
   - Deletes the marker (so a later session doesn't inherit the tag).
4. The agent runs the skills, the session ends naturally.
5. On the next `git commit`, the PostCommit hook condenses the review session into the checkpoint on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. The per-session metadata carries `Kind: "agent_review"` and `ReviewSkills`; the root `CheckpointSummary` sets `HasReview: true` as the umbrella flag.

This means `entire review` has no new commit type, no new branch, no new condensation path — it piggybacks on the existing session → checkpoint → commit pipeline.

## Flow inside `runReview`

1. **Pre-flight** — must be in a git repo.
2. **Load config** — reads `.entire/settings.json`. Malformed file surfaces an error instead of silently overwriting the user's other settings.
3. **First-run picker** — if `review` config is missing, `runReviewConfigPicker` shows a `huh` multi-select per installed agent (only agents with curated skills in `curatedReviewSkills` are offered) and writes the selection back.
4. **Agent selection** — `selectReviewAgent(review, --agent)`. With `--agent NAME`, picks that specific agent; otherwise alphabetically-first.
5. **Hooks-installed gate** — aborts with a clear "run `entire configure --agent <name>` first" if the selected agent has no hooks installed (since nothing would ever adopt the marker).
6. **Re-run guard** — reads HEAD's `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, resolves the checkpoint summary, checks `HasReview`. If the current HEAD is already reviewed, prompt "Already reviewed… proceed anyway?"
7. **Resolve HEAD SHA + worktree root** and write the pending marker.
8. **`--track-only` branch** — prints "marker written; start the agent manually" and returns. Marker persists.
9. **Resolve `Launcher`** — if the selected agent has no `LaunchCmd` (cursor, opencode, copilot-cli, factoryai-droid), fall back to the same persist-marker behavior as `--track-only`. *Critically, this happens before the cleanup defer* so the marker survives for the user to adopt manually.
10. **Cleanup defer** — on any error/exit past this point, if the marker is still there (the hook never adopted it — agent crashed, user `/quit`ed immediately), clear it so it doesn't mis-tag an unrelated future session.
11. **Print scope** — a one-line `reviewScope` summary (branch vs base, ahead commits, files changed, uncommitted) via `git` shell-outs.
12. **Compose prompt** (`"Please run these review skills in order: 1. X 2. Y"`) and launch the agent subprocess.

## Flags

- `--edit` — re-open the picker to modify the saved config.
- `--track-only` — write the marker without spawning the agent (for when you want to start the agent yourself).
- `--agent NAME` — pick a specific configured agent when you've configured more than one.

## Where things live

- Command: `cmd/entire/cli/review.go`
- Marker adoption in the hook: `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:271-289`
- `Launcher` interface: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/agent.go` (implemented by `claudecode`, `codex`, `geminicli`)
- Per-agent hook install/check: `cmd/entire/cli/agent/<name>/hooks.go`
- Settings schema: `EntireSettings.Review map[string][]string` in `cmd/entire/cli/settings/settings.go`
- Checkpoint fields: `Kind`, `ReviewSkills` on `CommittedMetadata`; `HasReview` on `CheckpointSummary` — both in `cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/`

## Settings example

```json
{
  "review": {
    "claude-code": ["/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr", "/test-auditor"],
    "codex": ["/codex:adversarial-review"]
  }
}
```

Keys are registry agent names. Values are skill invocations passed verbatim to the agent in the composed initial prompt.

Example contents after `entire review --track-only` in a configured repo:

```json
{
  "agent_name": "claude-code",
  "skills": [
    "/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr",
    "/test-auditor"
  ],
  "starting_sha": "9411f0c48abc123...",
  "started_at": "2026-04-22T11:30:00Z",
  "worktree_path": "/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli"

```

It's the same marker written whether you use `--track-only`, the default spawn path, or the non-launchable-agent fallback — the only difference is who clears it. In the spawn path, the cleanup defer clears it if the agent exits before firing `UserPromptSubmit`; in `--track-only` and the launcher fallback, the defer isn't registered, so the marker persists until whichever agent session's `UserPromptSubmit` hook adopts it first.

Two things to note:

- It lives under `.git/entire-sessions/` (shared across worktrees), *not* under `.entire/`. That's why `WorktreePath` is on the struct: multiple worktrees share the same marker directory, so an agent session in worktree B must not claim a marker written by `entire review` in worktree A. The adoption check at `review.go:173-178` skips the marker if the worktree paths don't match.
- Only one marker exists at a time. A second `entire review` overwrites the first.

Because `entire review` and the agent's session hooks are **different processes** that don't share state.

The handoff problem:

- **`entire review`** knows the answer to *what* (agent, skills, worktree) but not *where* (the session ID doesn't exist yet — the agent hasn't started).
- **The session hook** (fired later, as a fresh `entire hooks <agent> user-prompt-submit` subprocess invoked by the agent) knows *where* (it has the session ID) but not *what* (it has no idea whether this session is a review).

They need to meet somewhere. The marker is that meeting point — a tiny file on disk written by the former, read by the latter.

## Why not the obvious alternatives

**Environment variable.** You'd set `ENTIRE_REVIEW=1` when spawning the agent. But the agent's hook is invoked as a *separate* process spawned by the agent itself — not a child of `entire review`. Whether your env var reaches that grandchild depends on the agent's internal plumbing, and some agents (cursor, opencode via JSON hook configs) don't pass environment through at all. Not portable across agents.

**Agent-specific CLI flags.** You could pass `--review-mode` when launching Claude Code, and the agent could tell its hooks. But this requires per-agent cooperation, breaks for non-launchable agents (where the user starts the agent manually), and doesn't exist as a contract in any of the agent CLIs.

**Use the session ID.** `entire review` doesn't know it yet — the session is created when the agent starts, *after* the command has returned.

**Check session state after the fact.** You'd have to scan newly-created sessions and retroactively tag one as a review. But which one? Concurrent sessions in the same directory make this ambiguous, and you'd tag the wrong session if the user opened a non-review Claude window between `entire review` and their real review session.

**Commit trailer.** Nothing has been committed yet.

## What the marker actually solves

1. **Cross-process state** with a trivially reliable medium (one small JSON file, `.git/entire-sessions/` is already the state directory used by the rest of the strategy).
2. **Late binding**: the review intent is declared before the session exists, and gets applied to *whichever* session starts next in that worktree.
3. **Worktree scoping**: `WorktreePath` on the marker is the mechanism that prevents a non-review session in worktree B from claiming a marker written for worktree A.
4. **Self-cleanup**: adoption deletes the marker, so leftover state from a crashed command doesn't silently tag a future unrelated session.

It's the minimum-viable handoff — smaller than you could do with any of the alternatives, and agnostic to which agent you're using.

message.content: I wonder if it makes more sense to rather attach the session as review if you want to do a review manually then do `--track-only` and then make sure you run the session right after...

content.text:
Reasonable design — and honestly probably better for the manual case. The current `--track-only` has an awkward property: it sits in a state where "the next session in this worktree becomes a review", which creates a small footgun window. If you write the marker and then accidentally open an unrelated Claude window before your intended review session, that unrelated session eats the marker.

An `entire review --attach` flow would invert that: do the review in whatever session you want, then tag it explicitly by session ID. No race, no sitting state, no "did my marker get claimed by the wrong session?" worry.

## The main tradeoffs

**Skills list.** The marker carries `Skills` into the adoption step, which ends up in `CommittedMetadata.ReviewSkills`. An attach flow needs to source that somewhere — options are (a) a `--skills` flag, (b) read from saved config, or (c) drop the skills record and just tag `Kind=agent_review`. (c) is tempting but loses the audit trail ("which skills actually ran?"). (b) is the most ergonomic but only works if the user stuck to configured skills.

**Timing window.** Attach must happen before the PostCommit hook condenses the session. Condensation is triggered by `git commit`; a session that's been committed has its metadata frozen on `entire/checkpoints/v1`. Mutating a condensed session means rebuilding the checkpoint tree and writing a new commit on that branch — doable but an order of magnitude more code than mutating session state.

**Session disambiguation.** "Attach to which session?" — most-recent-active in current worktree is the obvious answer, but concurrent sessions make this a real question. The marker design sidesteps it because it's the session that *claims* the marker, not the command that *picks* the session.

**Lost signal.** Pre-declaration is a small commitment device — "I'm about to review" vs. "I already reviewed, trust me." Not a strong argument against attach; the condensed metadata is the source of truth either way.

## My take

Keep spawn-with-marker as the default (the `entire review` with no flags path) — it works cleanly when `entire review` launches the agent, and the hook adoption is unambiguous. 

Drop `--track-only`, add `--attach` for the manual case. The attach flow needs one decision: whether to require `--skills` or default to the configured skills for the selected agent. I'd start with "read from configured skills, error if none configured, allow `--skills` override" — keeps UX consistent with the spawn flow.

## Shape

```
entire attach <session-id>             # existing
entire attach <session-id> --review    # new: also tag as agent_review
```

Implementation is small:

1. Add a `--review` bool flag (and optionally `--skills` for the skills list; default to the configured skills for the resolved agent, error if none).
2. In `runAttach`, when the flag is set, pass `Kind: session.KindAgentReview` and `ReviewSkills: skills` into the `WriteCommittedOptions` passed to `checkpoint.WriteCommitted`. The summary's `HasReview = true` derivation already falls out of the existing `state.Kind.IsReview()` seam.

With `attach --review` in place, `entire review` shrinks back to just the spawn path:

- Default: launch configured agent with the review prompt, marker-based adoption (unchanged — it's the clean path).
- `--edit`: reopen the picker.

And it removes the cleanup defer and the worktree-path scoping logic on the marker, since the marker only needs to live during the spawned-agent's short lifetime — or not exist at all if we decide spawn also uses attach-style post-hoc tagging.

The spawn path can't easily move to post-hoc attach because the command would need to know the session ID, which is generated inside the agent — the same reason the marker exists today. So: keep the marker for spawn, use `attach --review` for manual. Two paths, each minimal.

I like it — `skills` is a leaky abstraction. It assumes a review is a list of slash commands, but really what we want to record is "what the reviewer actually asked." That's the composed prompt for spawn, and the first user prompt for attach. One concept, two sources.

## What would change

**Storage.** `ReviewSkills []string` → `ReviewPrompt string` on:
- `session.State`
- `checkpoint.WriteCommittedOptions` + `CommittedMetadata`
- `PendingReviewMarker`
- JSON field `"review_skills"` → `"review_prompt"` (no back-compat concern — feature is unreleased)

**Settings.** `review: map[string][]string` → `review: map[string]string`. Per agent, one string. Simple case stays trivial (`"claude-code": "/pr-review-toolkit:review-pr"`), complex case works (`"claude-code": "Please review and run /test-auditor, then /silent-failure-hunter"`).

**Spawn path.** `composeReviewPrompt([]string)` goes away; the prompt is already the prompt. `runReview` just passes `review[agentName]` straight to `launcher.LaunchCmd(ctx, prompt)` and stores it on the marker.

**Attach path.** Pulls the session's first user prompt from the transcript (we already parse transcripts in attach — `ag.ReadTranscript` + there's existing prompt extraction for `meta.FirstPrompt` at `attach.go:147`). Stores that as `ReviewPrompt`.

You gain flexibility (prompts can express workflow, not just command lists) and unified semantics (spawn and attach record the same shape). You lose structured queryability — today `review_skills: ["/a", "/b"]` is grep-friendly for "which reviews ran `/test-auditor`?" With prompts, that becomes substring match. For audit/reporting purposes, that's a real regression, though one you might not care about yet.

Two new commits added on top of the previous four:

- **`7d9aadb91` Record the composed review prompt on session and checkpoint metadata** — adds `ReviewPrompt string` alongside `ReviewSkills` on `session.State`, `PendingReviewMarker`, `WriteCommittedOptions`, and `CommittedMetadata`. Spawn path composes the prompt once and stores it on the marker. No behavior change yet — just the field plumbing.

- **`2505c5fd2` Add review-attach surfaces for post-hoc review tagging** — introduces `attachOptions` struct, the `--review` + `--skills` flags on `entire attach`, and the `entire review attach <id>` subcommand. Both paths funnel through `runAttach` with review fields set; skills resolve from `--skills` or configured `settings.Review[agent]`, erroring if neither is set. Existing-checkpoint sessions are refused with a concrete error since rewriting condensed metadata isn't implemented yet. Five new tests cover the runAttach path, both command surfaces, the already-checkpointed error, and the no-skills-configured error.
